qt: to the Commission Dario Nardella (S&D), Sandro Gozi (Renew), Nicola Zingaretti (S&D), Giorgio Gori (S&D), Marco Tarquinio (S&D), Brando Benifei (S&D), Stefano Bonaccini (S&D), Alessandro Zan (S&D), Irene Tinagli (S&D), Bernard Guetta (Renew), Pina Picierno (Renew), Christophe Grudler (Renew), Dainius Žalimas (Renew), Lucia Yar (Renew), Elisabetta Gualmini (Renew) Subject:

On 14 October 2026, the same day that Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu began presenting his defence in court, Turkish authorities seized Halk TV, an independent, pro-opposition news channel, pursuant to a judicial order. The channel, which had reported on İmamoğlu’s trial and corruption allegations against the ruling party, was taken off air, journalists were barred from the premises, and its social media accounts were blocked. The Savings Deposit Insurance Fund was appointed as trustee instead1. This incident reflects a broader pattern of restrictions on independent media in Türkiye, raising serious concerns across several areas, including freedom of expression and the rule of law, as also highlighted by the Commission’s Türkiye Report 20252. In the light of the above, given the existing framework of EU-Türkiye relations and its status as a candidate country: 1.
Does the Commission intend to act in response to these developments and, if so, what concrete measures will it take?

Does the Commission consider Türkiye’s current situation to constitute ‘significant regression or persistent lack of progress’ in the areas referred to in Article 8(4) of Regulation (EU) 2021/1529, within the meaning of Article 8(5)?
Will the Commission reduce or interrupt EU pre-accession financial and economic assistance accordingly?

Human Rights Watch, https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/10/14/turkish-government-takes-overindependent-tv-news-channel. 2 Commission staff working document of 4 November 2025 entitled ‘Türkiye 2025 Report’, https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/document/download/4bb4ddd1-4f20-4ee0-92db926996ec8dd1_en?filename=t%C3%BCrkiye-report-2025.pdf. 1
